kings2.3.p1.b1.text: … Jehoram son of Ahab became king of Israel, and he reigned in Samaria twelve years.

kings2.3.p1.b2.text: Now Mesha king of Moab was a sheep breeder, … But after the death of Ahab, the king of Moab rebelled against the king of Israel.

kings2.3.p1.b3.text: I will go … I am like you, my people are your people, and my horses are your horses.

kings2.3.p1.b4.text: By way of the Desert of Edom

kings2.3.p2.b1.text: … after they had traveled a roundabout route for seven days, they had no water for their army or for their animals.

kings2.3.p2.b2.text: Alas … for the LORD has summoned these three kings to deliver them into the hand of Moab!

kings2.3.p2.b3.text: Is there no prophet of the LORD here? Let us inquire of the LORD through him.

kings2.3.p2.b4.text: Elisha son of Shaphat is here. He used to pour water on the hands of Elijah.

kings2.3.p3.b1.text: What have we to do with each other? Go to the prophets of your father and of your mother!

kings2.3.p3.b2.text: … were it not for my regard for the presence of Jehoshaphat king of Judah, I would not look at you or acknowledge you.

kings2.3.p3.b3.text: But now, bring me a harpist.

kings2.3.p3.b4.text: And while the harpist played, the hand of the LORD came upon Elisha

kings2.3.p4.b1.text: This is what the LORD says: ‘Dig this valley full of ditches.’ For the LORD says, ‘You will not see wind or rain, but the valley will be filled with water, and you will drink—you and your cattle and your animals.’

kings2.3.p4.b2.text: You will not see wind or rain …

kings2.3.p4.b3.text: The next morning, at the time of the morning sacrifice, water suddenly flowed from the direction of Edom and filled the land.

kings2.3.p5.b1.text: Now all the Moabites had heard that the kings had come up to fight against them. So all who could bear arms, young and old, were summoned and stationed at the border.

kings2.3.p5.b2.text: This is blood! … The kings have clashed swords and slaughtered one another. Now to the plunder, Moab!

kings2.3.p5.b3.text: But when the Moabites came to the camp of Israel, the Israelites rose up and attacked them, and they fled before them.

kings2.3.p6.b1.text: They destroyed the cities, and each man threw stones on every good field until it was covered. They stopped up every spring and cut down every good tree. …

kings2.3.p6.b2.text: When the king of Moab saw that the battle was too fierce for him, he took with him seven hundred swordsmen to break through to the king of Edom, but they could not prevail.

kings2.3.p6.b3.text: So he took his firstborn son, who was to succeed him, and offered him as a burnt offering on the city wall.

kings2.3.p6.b4.text: And there was great fury against the Israelites, so they withdrew and returned to their own land.
